sentences.text: The present application was listed on 10th July, 2025, on which date after considering the medical report dated 5th May, 2025 of the Senior Medical Officer, Central Jail, Tihar the Court had directed the Appellant to be examined by a medical Board constituted by AIIMS, New Delhi.
The report dated 30th July, 2025 of the said medical Board is on record.

After having perused the said report,
the Court had directed vide order dated 31st July, 2025 that the Appellant be produced on the next date as also for one of the doctors of the medical Board to remain present virtually.
6. Today, Dr. Arvind Kumar from AIIMS has joined the proceedings virtually and briefed the Court about the medical condition of the Appellant.

As per the medical Board's report, the diagnosis and current medical condition of the Appellant is as under:
"The following are the findings, including the diagnosis and current medical condition of Mr. Vikas Kumar, as determined by the Medical Board during the medical examination.
1. Diabetes Mellitus : Controlled on Oral Medication 2.
Systemic Hypertension: Controlled on Oral Medication "
3. Migraine without aura: Controller on Oral Medication 4.

Right foot Neurofibromatosis with post amputation 4th toe (may years back), with no signs of cellulitis - advised foot care, nail care, limb elevation, crepe bandage on OPD basis through the local medical facility - No reconstructive surgery is needed at present.
5. For Right foot - To continue footwear modification which was earlier advised from Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation OPD."
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 09/08/2025 at 00:13:38 7.
The Appellant has also been produced before the Court today and he has made some submissions about his medical conditions.

The Appellant submits that he wishes to consult doctors at Max Hospital in Delhi as also one Dr. John Mukopadhyay, who as per the Appellant is a consultant at Paras Hospital, Patna and also runs his own clinic.
The Appellant submits that in the past he had consulted and had undergone treatment as prescribed by Dr. Mukopadhyay 8.
The Court has heard the parties and perused the documents on record including the medical report from AIIMS as also the latest Nominal Roll of the Appellant.

He is undergoing life imprisonment.

10. Considering the above, this Court is of the opinion that on medical ground, the Appellant is entitled to an interim suspension of sentence and release on interim bail for a period of four weeks from the date of his release, subject to furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.20,000/- with a surety of the like amount, to the satisfaction of the Trial Court/Link Court.

The Appellant shall be released subject to the following further conditions:
(i) The Appellant shall remain in Delhi and Patna to seek his medical treatment.
The Appellant shall intimate the concerned Investigating Officer of his address in Delhi and Patna and also when he leaves Delhi for Patna and shall keep him informed about his location.
(ii) The Appellant shall report to the concerned CBI office in Patna or CBI Office Delhi, as per his location, twice a week i.e., on every Tuesday and Friday at 11:00 AM.
The concerned officer is directed to release him by

(iii) The Appellant shall provide his mobile number to the concerned Investigating Officer and keep it operational at all times so that the Investigating Officer can contact him and ascertain his location.
The Appellant shall also inform the concerned Investigating Officer about any change in his mobile number.
(iv) The Appellant states that he does not have a passport.
Accordingly, he shall not leave the country without prior permission of this Court.
(v) The Appellant shall intimate this Court, by way of an affidavit, as also the concerned Investigating Officer regarding any change in the residential address in Patna and Delhi.
(vi) The Appellant shall appear before this Court as and when the matter is taken up for hearing either virtually or physically.
11. The Appellant shall surrender before the concerned Jail Superintendent immediately upon expiry of the interim bail period.
12. Copy of the order be communicated to the concerned Jail Superintendent for necessary information and compliance.
13. The order be uploaded on the website of this Court forthwith.
